title: The Family Club
text: Hawthorn calls itself the Family Club, and the members hold it to that. They want the whole list at a family day this week, kids' clinic and all, on what was meant to be a main training day.

choices.label: Give them the whole day

effects.why: You gave the Family Club its day

choices.result: Kids in brown and gold everywhere. The main session goes out the window.

choices.label: Send the leadership group only

effects.hit_result: Some members felt snubbed and said so to the board.

choices.result: The rest of the list trains as planned. The families wanted the whole group.

title: Merger whispers
text: Money is tight, and a newspaper reports the league would welcome Hawthorn merging with a struggling Melbourne club. Old members are already ringing talkback, and the press wants to know where the coach stands.

choices.label: Say Hawthorn stands alone

effects.why: The coach stood with the members

choices.result: The members cheer. The board wanted the door left open.

choices.label: Say that's a matter for the board

effects.why: The coach wouldn't stand with the members

choices.result: The board is relieved. The rooms wanted to hear the coach say it.

title: The old guard wants the rooms
text: One of the club's hard men from the old days wants to address the players before a big game: who the club is, and what its members gave to keep it alive. He is fiery, and he goes long.

choices.label: Give him the rooms

effects.why: An old Hawk told them what the jumper cost

choices.result: The players come out roaring. Some of them are fired up, not switched on.

choices.label: Thank him and keep the rooms to the coaches

effects.why: Game day stayed about the plan

choices.result: Game day goes as planned. The old guard notices.

title: Do something!
text: A club great's three-quarter-time speech is the most quoted in Hawthorn's history: stop thinking, stop hoping, do. The players want your own version before this final.

choices.label: Give the speech
choices.result: The room is on its feet. If it goes wrong, the speech will be replayed all week.

choices.label: Keep it about the plan

effects.why: You kept them on the plan

choices.result: Calm, clear and about the plan. The players wanted fire.

title: Back to Glenferrie
text: Glenferrie Oval is still the club's spiritual home. The heritage committee asks for one open session there: old grandstand, old members, local kids.

choices.label: Run an open session at Glenferrie

effects.why: The players trained at the club's old home

choices.result: The old stand is full. It's a light session for the crowd.

choices.label: Keep the session closed
choices.result: A full, hard session behind closed gates. The heritage committee is disappointed.

title: Home games away from home
text: A regional government offers the club serious money to play some home games in its heartland, a long trip away. The board loves the money; the players hate the travel.

choices.label: Sign the deal
choices.result: The deal is done and the money's in. The first trip is in the players' legs.

choices.label: Keep every home game in Melbourne
choices.result: The players are pleased. The board sees the money walk away.

title: The curse
text: At a dinner, the club president says Geelong don't have the mental drive to beat Hawthorn. It's on every back page by morning, and the Cats have pinned it up.

choices.label: Back the president
choices.result: The players love it. Lose, and the Cats will rub it in.

choices.label: Keep the coaches out of it

effects.why: The coaches let the footy do the talking

choices.result: The coaches say nothing. The president isn't happy.

title: Bad blood with the Bombers
text: The papers dig up the old Hawthorn and Essendon wars: brawls, big finals, no love lost. Radio wants a line from you, and the players want to know if they're expected to stand up.

choices.label: Say we won't take a backward step
choices.result: The players are up for it. The league and the board are not impressed.

choices.label: Say it's a game of footy
choices.result: A calm line for the radio. Some players wanted more.

title: A long offer from interstate
text: A cashed-up interstate club has offered {name} a deal far longer than you would ever give. He likes it here, but he has told his manager to listen.

choices.label: Match the length
choices.result: {first} stays. The board winces at what he'll be paid in the last years.

choices.label: Hold your offer

effects.why: The club wouldn't match the length he was offered

choices.result: No long deal on the books. {first} hears what the club thinks he's worth.

title: Trade the pick, chase the flag
text: Hawthorn has a habit of trading young picks for proven players when the window is open. The list manager has a mature midfielder lined up for your first-round pick.

choices.label: Do the trade

effects.why: You traded for the flag now

choices.result: A proven midfielder arrives. The young players see one fewer spot to fight for.

choices.label: Keep the pick

effects.why: The club backed its own pathway

choices.result: The pick stays. The board wanted the window pushed.

title: The board won't say rebuild
text: Hawthorn rarely bottoms out, and the board says it never will. After missing the finals, they want you to promise September next year, not a rebuild.

choices.label: Promise finals
choices.result: The board is happy. Every loss next year will be measured against that promise.

choices.label: Ask for time to rebuild
choices.result: The young players get their chance. The board doesn't like the word.

title: Are the Hawks tanking?
text: A journalist claims the club is resting fit senior players to slide down the ladder for a better pick. The league has asked questions.

choices.label: Pick your best side

effects.why: The club played its best side every week

choices.result: The senior men are back. The kids lose their games.

choices.label: Keep backing the kids
choices.result: The kids keep playing. The questions keep coming.

title: Hawthorn can kick
text: Hawthorn sides are known for their kicking. The skills coach wants every session to open with a long, hard kicking block, even in a heavy week.

choices.label: Every session, no exceptions

effects.why: Hawthorn kicks well, every day

choices.result: The kicking is crisp. The legs are tired by Saturday.

choices.label: Only on light days
choices.result: Fresh legs on game day, and less work on the skills.

title: Boring Hawthorn
text: The press says your defensive zone is choking the life out of footy, and supporters on talkback agree.

choices.label: Defend the method

effects.why: The coach backed the way we play

choices.result: The players back the method. Talkback keeps at it.

choices.label: Promise to open it up
choices.result: The supporters like the sound of it. The players aren't sure of the plan.

title: The reserves need you
text: The reserves have a final this weekend, and their coach asks for {name}, who missed senior selection.

choices.label: Send him
choices.result: {first} plays a final for the twos. He'll carry it into next week.

choices.label: Keep him fresh
choices.result: {first} rests. He wanted the game.

title: The membership drive
text: Hawthorn chases a membership record most years. Marketing wants three players at member events every night this week.

choices.label: Send them
choices.result: The members love it. Three tired players drag through the week.

choices.label: One event, one player
choices.result: The side trains as planned. Marketing is disappointed.

title: The pokies question
text: The club's poker-machine venues pay a lot of the bills. Anti-gambling groups and some members want the club out, and the board asks the coach to take a stand in front of the members.

choices.label: Back getting out

effects.why: The coach stood with the members on the pokies

choices.result: The members applaud. The board counts the money it may lose.

choices.label: Stay out of it

effects.why: The coach ducked the members' question

choices.result: The board is relieved. Some members wanted a stand.

title: A year too early
text: {name} wants one more year. Hawthorn's way has long been to move a player on a year too early rather than a year too late, and the list manager wants to keep it that way. The rooms are watching.

choices.label: Give him the year

effects.why: The club looked after a servant

choices.result: {first} gets one more year. The rooms approve.

choices.label: Retire him with honour

effects.why: The club stuck to a year too early
The club moved him on before he was ready

choices.result: A guard of honour and a farewell. The senior men take note.

title: A new home
text: The club wants to build a training and community base on reclaimed land on the city's edge. The president asks the coach to front the members' appeal and give up two training days to it.

choices.label: Front the appeal
choices.result: The appeal flies. Two training days are gone.

choices.label: Leave it to the board
choices.result: Training goes as planned. The president wanted his coach out front.

title: The premiership reunion
text: One of the club's premiership sides holds its reunion at the club. Its stars want to run drills with the current players and tell them what it took.

choices.label: Let them run the session

effects.why: Premiership players showed them what it took

choices.result: Old drills and hard words. The players lap it up.

choices.label: A lunch, not a session
choices.result: Training goes as planned. The old premiership men wanted to get on the track.

title: Best and fairest night
text: At the best and fairest, {name} wants to use his speech to call out the side's standards in front of the families and sponsors.

choices.label: Let him say it

effects.why: A leader called out the standards in public

choices.result: The room goes quiet. Everyone heard it.

choices.label: Ask him to keep it a celebration

effects.why: You softened your message

choices.result: A happy night. {first} thinks something needed saying.

title: They want your assistant
text: Hawthorn assistants keep becoming senior coaches elsewhere. A rival club wants your best line coach as its senior coach.

choices.label: Give him your blessing

effects.why: The club was proud to see one of its own go up

choices.result: He goes with the club's blessing. His line loses his work.

choices.label: Try to keep him with a bigger role

miss.why: He left anyway, and it ended badly

effects.hit_result: He stays, and his line keeps improving.
effects.miss_result: He goes anyway, and the parting is cold.

choices.result: A bigger role and a bigger pay packet on the table.

title: Commando camp
text: Hawthorn's hard men of old trained like commandos. The leadership group wants a punishing preseason camp in the bush.

choices.label: Run the camp

effects.why: They survived the commando camp together

choices.result: Mud, hills and no sleep. The legs are still heavy come round one.

choices.label: Run a team-building weekend instead

effects.why: A weekend away brought the group closer

choices.result: A good weekend away. Not much hard work done.

title: Son of a Hawk
text: A premiership Hawk's son is eligible as a father-son pick. He's raw and a long way off senior footy, and the members want him in brown and gold.

choices.label: Take him

effects.why: A premiership family stays in brown and gold
A pick went on loyalty, not the best available

choices.result: The members are thrilled. The recruiters wanted someone readier.

choices.label: Pass on him

effects.why: The pick went on the best player available

choices.result: The pick goes on the best available. The members are not happy.
